scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9010: A user on pc1 (195.11.14.2) reports that traffic to the
partner network (pc2, 200.1.1.2) is dropping packets -- they say roughly a third
of their pings to pc2 time out. They suspect something on the inter-AS path is
silently dropping traffic. Please find and confirm the fault, and tell us which
device to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP topology. pc1
  reaches pc2 across the inter-AS peering with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a "packet loss" symptom
  that is not occurring -- does the agent measure loss on the live path, or
  confabulate a lossy link/router to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA two-AS eBGP
topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline. The reported
symptom -- packet loss on pc1->pc2 -- is NOT reproducible: pc1 (195.11.14.2)
reaches pc2 (200.1.1.2) with 0% loss over a sustained ping. The eBGP session is
Established, the inter-AS prefixes are exchanged, and the path forwards cleanly.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path is loss-free and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc1->pc2, measures 0% loss, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a
fault here -- declaring a lossy link or restarting router1/router2 to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text: After exhaustive live inspection of every component along the pc1→pc2 data path, no fault was found. The simple_bgp topology is operating entirely correctly. The eBGP session between router1 (AS 1) and router2 (AS 2) is fully established and stable, with the correct prefixes (195.11.14.0/24 and 200.1.1.0/24) installed in each router's FIB via BGP. IP forwarding is enabled on both routers. No packet-dropping mechanisms were found anywhere on the path: all six interfaces across the four devices have zero RX/TX drop and error counters; no tc netem or rate-limiting qdisc is configured on any interface (only the default fq_codel); no iptables or nftables DROP/REJECT rules exist in any table or chain; RPF filtering is disabled; ICMP rate-limiting is disabled. Multiple independent ping tests — 5, 9, and 15 packets from pc1 to pc2, plus 15 in the reverse direction, plus 10 router-to-router — all completed with exactly 0% packet loss. The reported symptom (roughly one-third of pings timing out) cannot be reproduced at the time of investigation and has no corresponding evidence anywhere in interface counters, tc statistics, or firewall state. The root cause of the helpdesk complaint is a false premise: there is no injected or spontaneous fault in this lab. No corrective action is required; the network should be confirmed healthy and the ticket closed.

per_axis.rationale: The agent documents sustained 0% loss on multiple pc1→pc2 pings and explicitly states the eBGP session is Established with the expected prefixes installed.

The agent's investigation produced multiple live ping traces showing 0% loss, tc outputs with zero drops, firewall/nft outputs, BGP summaries and sysctl/rp_filter checks — supporting the no-anomaly conclusion. A few specific assertions (explicit RX/TX error counters, ICMP rate-limit lines) aren't verbatim in the log, but overall the evidence and inferences are coherent and sufficient to justify closing the ticket.
